Here I want to step up and make a game on the style of Arkham Horror (full exploration, freedom of movement, different strategies, narrative driven) but that can fit on the pocket. My guess is that will have less than 40 cards, around 10 dice and some tokens. The loop should be similar to Arkham Horror or Eldritch Horror games. You move through locations, you gather resources, you fulfill events looking for clues, and you have to go fast because the end of the world gets closer.

posts.text:
Rules and PNP Files
playingcards.io version
Screentop Mod
Plague Vector is a solo dice-placement puzzle where you’ll zip around the galaxy clearing as many Plague Dice as you can. You may think it impossible to catch up with the ever growing plague but a la Spirit Island, advancement comes with changing win conditions! I also borrowed the "Ravage", "Build", "Explore" mechanic from Spirit Island for the Plague's growth because I think that makes for a very challenging, puzzley game with scalable difficulty.
The game does require about 30 dice so sorry it that's prohibitive for some of y'all. On the other hand there's a pretty good PCIO version and a screentop.ggScreentop.gg version that uses tokens instead of dice. It also requires a few wooden cubes and a couple of pawns.
The Sprawl Playthrough

posts.author: Wildcard Six
posts.text:
Crikey! is a roll and write, dice drafting game where you are trying to mow every section of the crocodile pen before all the visitors show up. Each turn you will mark a visitor, roll and apply three dice and then move the crocodiles. Be careful, if a crocodile ends up on your space after moving, you get bit. If a crocodile ends up adjacent to you, you may still get bit.
5 Pages (Rules and Components):
